items.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Never got to know Eddie and I was always such an admirer of his, he was wonderful.

ctx.x: I mean it was wonderful anyway but it wasn’t the kind of thing Woody was into, he was into much more of a straight swinging kind of thing. Mulligan was writing more

esoterically too, which is why he and Woody never really hit it off. I mean they probably hit it off as people but, you know, we were all much more interested in experimenting then. And Woody allowed you to do things but if stuff got too linear and too… that’s why Woody and Eddie Sauter never hit it off, whereas Artie and Eddie Sauter did. The strangest thing was Benny and Eddie Sauter but that was kind of shotgun wedding, it just so happened that it was Benny's new band in 19… when was it?

items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: that's where I met Johnny and encouraged him to go to Stefan... So he came back in '51 and Johnny got him to do the musical... suggesting we start a band.

ctx.x: John came from McKinley's band; he had been up at Yale with Miller and Miller didn't take him overseas because (inaudible), so Ray got him back to
write for him, and that's where I met Johnny and encouraged him to go to Stefan, which he did. He says he's always been grateful to me for that. I don't know why but he has been.
How long did you stay with Ray then?
